name: Peter A. Law
tagline: Top rated Personal Injury attorney in Atlanta, Georgia
about: Peter A. Law has an exemplary track record of securing favorable verdicts and settlements for personal injury victims. Mr. Law handles a variety of personal injury matters, including automobile accidents, premises liability, products liability, wrongful death and other tort cases. With numerous high-profile cases resulting in multimillion-dollar recoveries, he is known as one of Georgia’s top personal injury attorneys. Mr. Law is the senior principal of Law & Moran and accepts clients in the metro Atlanta area.

After graduating from Florida State University in 1990, Mr. Law earned his Juris Doctor in 1993 from the Emory University School of Law. He is admitted to practice law in Georgia and before the Court of Appeals of Georgia, the U.S. District Courts for the Northern and Middle Districts of Georgia, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit and the U.S. Supreme Court.

Mr. Law's achievements and strong business ethics have earned him the respect of his peers. In addition to receiving the highest rating of AV Preeminent* from Martindale-Hubbell, he is included annually in The Best Lawyers in America**. He has also been listed numerous times in Georgia Business Trend Magazine's Legal Elite list.

Mr. Law enjoys the opportunity to serve in leadership positions. He lectures frequently for various continuing legal education seminars and has written numerous articles on personal injury topics. He is an active member of several bars and associations, including the State Bar of Georgia, the American Association for Justice, the International Society of Barristers, and the International Academy of Trial Lawyers. Previously, Mr. Law served as regional vice president and co-chair of the Membership Committee of the Georgia Trial Lawyers Association.

*AV Preeminent and BV Distinguished are certification marks of Reed Elsevier Properties Inc., used in accordance with the Martindale-Hubbell certification procedures, standards and policies. Martindale-Hubbell is the facilitator of a peer review rating process. Ratings reflect the confidential opinions of members of the bar and the judiciary. Martindale-Hubbell ratings fall into two categories: legal ability and general ethical standards.
